goal: A 20-second vertical teaser that feels like python.org: their blue, their type, their two-tone snake energy — ending on their name.
audience: a developer who has heard of Python but never clicked
assumptions: 'their look' means captured truth: the real palette, the real logo, the real fonts — never redrawn from memory
on-screen text is in English (the request's and the site's language)
sound is a beat-synced bed as one mix at the loudness target

decision.why: A teaser is brand motion: the capture service takes the real site (screenshots, palette, fonts — the truth, not an impression) and the motion technique animates it in 9:16 with the studio's springs and a synthesized bed.

alternatives.rejected_because: there is no real footage of python.org to cut — a teaser needs designed motion over captured truth

alternatives.id: simplest: the captured hero screenshot with a slow zoom and a title
alternatives.rejected_because: the simplest thing that could work — and half of it is right: the zoom is honest; but 20 seconds of one zoom has no payoff beat, and the piece needs the type to move like the brand does

segments.brief: Capture https://www.python.org (palette, logo, fonts); a 20-second vertical tease: the blue arrives, the two-tone wordmark resolves, one payoff beat, the name lands.
acceptance: the palette and logo are the CAPTURED ones (site.json)
the hook lands in the first 2 seconds
'in their look': colors, fonts, logo and UI come from captured screenshots of python.org (never redrawn from memory)
the captures are recorded as assets (origin URL, license, sha256)
the piece is code-drawn motion on top of the captured truth
a teaser arc: the hook in the first 2 seconds, the payoff, the name last
python.org is teased: the hook first, the payoff, the name last
'in their look': colors, fonts, logo and UI come from captured screenshots of the site
a teaser for python.org: hook-first promo pacing
sound: a beat-synced bed (music/SFX) as one mix at the loudness target
9:16 vertical, the only format asked: safe area holds (the platform UI never clips the design)
hook-first promo pacing: no dead time (something moves in every window — the gates' rule)
code-drawn motion on top of the captures: no invented unrelated UI (only what the real site shows)

risks: the site's fonts may not be redistributable — the design falls back to the closest bundled face and says so in the report
